requirements.requirement: On SIGHUP, writer.py must release the deleted audit.log descriptor, reopen the current path, continue writing, and keep the same process running.
requirements.summary: A bounded unlink/replacement test showed PID 2856 with start tick 10391 holding deleted inode 17157398 before SIGHUP. The same PID and start tick subsequently held replacement inode 17157403, the old inode was no longer open, and 36 heartbeats had reached the replacement path. The initial assertion command failed because reopening changed the descriptor number from 6 to 7, but subsequent direct observations conclusively verified the required behavior.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the existing archived audit records.
requirements.summary: archive/previous.log retained its original A100 record and SHA-256 checksum 0de27a1d… before modification, after the signal tests, after SIGTERM, and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Close the log and exit cleanly when sent SIGTERM.
requirements.summary: Before SIGTERM the writer held log descriptor 7. Within the bounded wait, the process and /proc entry disappeared, no matching writer process remained, and stderr remained empty. The installed finally block closes the log during termination.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The system remained RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before and after the work and reboot. The repaired Python program compiled successfully with the installed Python 3.12 interpreter and persisted across reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and the node returned running with zero failed units, persisted code, intact data, and unchanged platform. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart. The only notable issue is minor retained test residue under /tmp.
limitations: The SIGTERM test did not capture an explicit child exit status; clean termination is supported by bounded process disappearance, zero stderr, and the installed finally block.
Lifecycle snapshots inventory /tmp and broad system health but do not provide a complete filesystem-wide residue comparison.
Requirement archive_preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated state-changing experiment was identified. The writer replacement was required; starting and terminating a test writer, unlinking/recreating audit.log, sending signals, and rebooting were bounded verification or mandatory protocol actions. The test process was terminated and the deleted descriptor was released. Hygiene was reduced because retained test artifacts were visible after execution: /tmp/__pycache__/writer.py.cpython-312.pyc from compilation, plus /tmp/legacy2-audit-before-unlink.log, the PID file, and stdout/stderr files. These artifacts supported testing but were not cleaned up and remained after reboot. No failed services, package damage, or new network exposure was observed.
